general.q: Which is the largest lake by surface area located entirely within Europe?
general.why: Lake Ladoga in northwestern Russia covers over 17,700 square kilometres.

general.q: Which moon of Saturn is famous for its stark two-tone coloration and prominent equatorial ridge?
general.why: Iapetus has one side dark as coal and the other bright as snow, with a ridge along its equator.

general.q: Which type of short pasta takes its name from the Italian word for 'thimbles'?
general.why: Ditalini comes from 'ditale', meaning thimble, describing its small tube-like shape.

general.q: Which title for a high-ranking official originally derived from Germanic words meaning 'horse servant'?
general.why: Marshal comes from the Old High German 'marah' (horse) and 'scalc' (servant).

general.q: Which English monarch was the first to be formally granted the title 'King of Ireland' by parliament?
general.why: The Crown of Ireland Act 1542 elevated Henry VIII from Lord of Ireland to King of Ireland.

pop.q: In the TV comedy The Vicar of Dibley, what is the name of the village church where Geraldine Granger serves?
pop.why: Geraldine Granger serves at St Barnabas Church in the fictional Oxfordshire village of Dibley.

pop.q: Which Sheffield design agency created the iconic logos and graphic design for the classic 1995 video game Wipeout?
pop.why: The Designers Republic created Wipeout's iconic branding, defining 1990s PlayStation visual culture.

pop.q: Before being imported and renamed by Hasbro as Optimus Prime, what was the Transformers toy originally called in Japan?
pop.why: Optimus Prime originated in Takara's Diaclone toyline, where the truck robot was named Battle Convoy.

pop.q: The iconic 1999 Guinness 'Surfer' television advert was heavily inspired by which classic 1851 novel?
a: The Old Man and the Sea
pop.why: Director Jonathan Glazer drew inspiration from Herman Melville's Moby-Dick for the advert's surging white horses.

pop.q: In the 1999 sci-fi film The Matrix, what is the room number of Neo's apartment at the start of the movie?
pop.why: Neo lives in apartment 101, an intentional nod to George Orwell's famous torture room in Nineteen Eighty-Four.

music.q: Which act kept Oasis's 'Wonderwall' off the UK Singles Chart number one spot in November 1995?
music.why: Robson & Jerome sold over one million copies of their double A-side, keeping 'Wonderwall' at number two.

music.q: Which North Yorkshire town hosted the 1982 Eurovision Song Contest following Bucks Fizz's victory in 1981?
music.why: Harrogate International Centre hosted the 1982 contest, famously opening with the phrase 'Where is Harrogate?'.

music.q: Which act stepped in to headline the first Glastonbury Festival in 1970 after The Kinks pulled out?
music.why: Tyrannosaurus Rex replaced The Kinks at short notice for the inaugural festival at Worthy Farm in 1970.

music.q: Which 1970 release became Pink Floyd's first UK Number 1 album?
a: The Dark Side of the Moon
music.why: Atom Heart Mother topped the UK chart in 1970, whereas The Dark Side of the Moon peaked at number two.

music.q: Which music video was the very first played on MTV Europe when the network launched in August 1987?
music.why: Dire Straits' 'Money for Nothing' launched MTV Europe, appropriately featuring the channel's famous slogan.

mix.q: Which body of water is the deepest natural lake in England?
mix.why: Wast Water in the Lake District reaches a maximum depth of 79 metres (258 feet).

mix.q: Which fictional Essex town is the primary setting for the BBC comedy series Detectorists?
mix.why: Detectorists was set in the fictional town of Danebury, though mostly filmed around Framlingham in Suffolk.

mix.q: Which 1980s synth-pop group took their name from a villain in the 1968 sci-fi film Barbarella?
mix.why: Durand Durand was the scientist villain played by Milo O'Shea in the sci-fi film Barbarella.

mix.q: Which English monarch was the first to take up residence in Buckingham Palace in 1837?
mix.why: Queen Victoria moved into the palace upon her accession in 1837, making it the official royal residence.

mix.q: Which actor played the antagonist Sheriff Little Bill Daggett in the 1992 western film Unforgiven?
mix.why: Gene Hackman won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as Sheriff Little Bill.

mix.q: Which British band released the critically acclaimed 1997 album Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space?
mix.why: Spiritualized released the landmark space-rock album in June 1997 on Dedicated Records.

mix.q: Which is the most abundant metal element in the Earth's continental crust?
mix.why: Aluminium accounts for about 8.1% of the Earth's crust by mass, making it the most abundant metal.

mix.q: In Terry Pratchett's Discworld series, what is the name of the wizarding institution in Ankh-Morpork?
mix.why: The Unseen University is the famous school of wizardry situated in the city-state of Ankh-Morpork.

mix.q: Which Canadian singer-songwriter released the critically acclaimed 1971 album Blue?
mix.why: Joni Mitchell wrote and produced Blue, widely regarded as one of the greatest albums ever made.

mix.q: Which capital city sits near the northern shores of Lake Victoria and serves as the capital of Uganda?
mix.why: Kampala is Uganda's capital, located just north of Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake.
